sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The Project Workbench is the primary workspace for Project Leads and the controller's deep-inspection surface for any project. It uses a master-detail layout: a project list on the left and a five-tab workspace on the right. The five tabs are **Overview / Forecast & Planning / Distribution / External Costs / Change History**. You can also arrive here via deep links from Portfolio Overview, Backlog, the Launchpad, or Capacity Management.

sections.title: Project List
sections.body: The left panel shows projects filtered by your role. Project Leads see their assigned projects (Anita owns 5: Master Data Hub Rollout, ERP Integration Phase 2, Sensor Data Pipeline, Predictive Maintenance PoC, Smart Logistics Pilot); Controllers see all 11 active + draft + planned. Each entry shows the project name, RAG indicator, type badge (Project / Service), and a status badge. Status badges are color-coded: amber for workflow statuses (Draft, Pending, CC Review, Changes Req.) and neutral for lifecycle statuses (Active, Completed, Planned).\n\nUse the **+ New** button at the top to create a new project draft (Project Leads only). The creation form collects project name, description, organizational entity (e.g., Business Unit), CapEx/OpEx classification, start/end months, and optional resource plan allocation.

sections.title: Overview Tab
sections.body:
The Overview tab is a tile grid summarising the project's health. Tiles include:
- **Project header** — name, hierarchy path, status, RAG, Stage badge, project type, t-shirt size, PL
- **Three-Point Summary** — Baseline / Forecast / Actuals YTD with Plan Drift and Execution Variance metrics
- **Milestone status** — current milestone with progress bar across the 5 lifecycle steps + next milestone
- **Resource Plan [year]** — total hours + top-3 roles + 'X more' aggregate
- **Cost mix** — CapEx / OpEx donut + Internal / External split
- **Progress tracker** — current milestone, intra-milestone %, deliverable checklist (X/N), confidence indicator (On track / At risk / Blocked), narrative
- **External costs** — total external EUR, vendor count, category breakdown bar (Consulting / Cloud-Infrastructure / Licenses / Travel)
- **Forecast health** — version number, cycle label, last-submission age, RAG indicator
- **Tech Navigator** — Complexity / Value / Composite scores + scatter chart anchor
- **Business-Transfer Charging** — Change/Run badge, BTC summary, **Open BTC tab** deep-link to `/charging?section=btc`

sections.title: 3-Point Comparison
sections.body: The Three-Point Summary tile (and the deeper variance waterfall it links to) shows three rows (Baseline, Forecast, Actuals) broken out by internal hours, external costs, and total. Variance columns show Plan Drift (forecast vs baseline), Execution Variance (actuals vs forecast), and Total Variance (actuals vs baseline). This gives a complete picture of where the project stands.

sections.title: Forecast & Planning Tab
sections.body:
In read mode, shows the current forecast grid with months as columns and resource roles + external cost types as rows. The grid uses **mixed granularity** per `[C-FG-07]`: monthly columns for the next 12 months (Apr-2026 through Mar-2027 in the demo), then quarterly columns out to the planning horizon. Quarter columns can be expanded into their three component months via **Expand all quarters**. Cells beyond the granularity boundary are flagged 'Provisional'.

Use the **Compare against** dropdown to overlay any prior `ForecastVersion` (e.g., v1 vs current) — changed cells render with green / red / blue colour coding. New `ForecastVersion` snapshots are written automatically on cycle close and on CR approval; manual snapshots are not part of the workflow.

Internal resource roles with employee assignments are expandable: click the role name to reveal which employees are assigned per month with their allocated hours. Use the 'Expand All Resources' / 'Collapse All Resources' button above the grid to toggle all role expansions at once.

**Auto-Allocation:** The system automatically assigns employees to internal resource lines so that allocation hours match forecast hours. When a project is approved or a change request is accepted, allocations are created or updated automatically. People already allocated to the project are preferred for consistency; additional people are selected deterministically from the matching role pool.

To edit, click **Rolling Forecast Review** to start the 5-phase Monthly Forecast Wizard (see next section).

**Check Availability slide-over (v5.2 W6):** Project Leads can open the Capacity role-availability grid as a 50%-viewport slide-over without leaving the Workbench — click **Check availability** in the F&P actions cluster (next to Rolling Forecast Review). The drawer shows the same scope controls + KPI summary + grid + role detail panel as the standalone `/capacity/availability` page. Selecting a slot's **Request this role** button closes the drawer and populates a banner above the grid with the captured role / location / suggested period; the banner has Edit / Clear (×) controls. See the Capacity Management manual for the full availability view.

sections.title: Monthly Forecast Wizard
sections.body:
The 5-phase wizard walks the PL through a forecast cycle submission. The phase stepper shows: **1 Retrospective · 2 Suggestions · 3 Edit Forecast · 4 Review · 5 Confirmation**.

**Phase 1 (Retrospective):** Review last month's forecast vs actuals. Variances > 10% are flagged; the **Acknowledge & Continue** button is disabled until each flagged row has an explanation in the free-text field. All monetary values are shown in full EUR format (e.g. 4.715 €).

**Phase 2 (Suggestions):** System shows AI-generated insights based on trends, burn rates, and utilization patterns. Apply or dismiss each suggestion. May be skipped if no suggestions are produced (per SPEC-003).

**Phase 3 (Edit Forecast):** Edit the forecast grid directly — both hours and external costs, monthly + quarterly. If no changes are needed, use the **Keep as is** button to proceed without modifications.

**Phase 4 (Review):** See all changes grouped by category with old / new / delta values in full EUR format. Add justification text.

**Phase 5 (Confirmation):** Click **Submit** — the system writes a new `ForecastVersion` snapshot (`version_type='cycle'`) and creates one or more CRs routed to the controller (and to the CC Owner first if internal resource changes are present).

**Forecast Locking:** While a CR is pending review (at any stage — controller, CC Owner, or sent back for changes), the **Rolling Forecast Review** button is disabled with a status indicator showing the CR number and its current approval stage. This prevents overlapping CRs for the same project. The full step-by-step is in `docs/workflows/03-forecast-cycle.md` (W03.1).

sections.title: Distribution Tab
sections.body:
Per-project view of Stage 1 inter-service distribution edges per `[F-S1-01..05]`. Shows the project's chargeable entity as the source / destination of cost-allocation edges, with each edge's percentage and the resulting effective cost flow. From this tab you can:
- See incoming distribution edges (cost being charged into this project from upstream services)
- See outgoing distribution edges (cost being passed downstream — typically only for offerings / internal services in the Run portfolio; Change-portfolio projects rarely distribute outward)
- Open the global Distribution editor at `/charging?section=distribution` for cross-project edits

The sum-rule per `[F-S1-02]` enforces that an entity's outgoing percentages plus its `to_business_pct` cannot exceed 100%. The remainder is treated as self-retained cost. See `docs/workflows/07-charging.md` (W07.1, W07.2) for the global editor walks.

sections.title: External Costs Tab
sections.body:
Per-project external-spend ledger. Rows are external cost line items broken out by `ExternalCostType` (Consulting, Cloud-Infrastructure, Licenses, Hardware, Travel, Other) and CapEx / OpEx classification. Columns are months matching the forecast grid's granularity. Shows forecast vs actuals per month with vendor attribution where available.

The **Total external (forecast)** KPI on the Overview tab's 'External costs' tile is the sum of all forecast values in this tab; the YTD actuals chip is the sum of all actuals values for months ≤ current cycle. Vendor count is the distinct count of vendors associated with actuals rows.

External cost types are admin-managed per `[E-08e]`/`[E-08f]` — see Administration → Reference Catalogues → External Cost Types.

sections.title: Change History Tab
sections.body:
Shows the chronological log of all change requests for this project (newest first). Each CR row displays its status badge, category, summary, cost impact, timestamp, submitter, and whether it was system-suggested.

**Sent-Back CRs:** Change requests returned by the controller are highlighted with an amber border, amber background, a warning icon, and an **Action Required** badge. Expanding a sent-back CR shows an inline diff view instead of the normal grid.

**Diff View for Sent-Back CRs:** When the controller has requested changes, expanding the CR reveals:
- **Controller Feedback** banner (amber) with the controller's comments explaining why changes were made
- **KPI Strip** showing Affected Lines (Current), Affected Lines (Proposed), and Total Impact
- **Color-coded comparison grid** with collapsible year columns: green cells for reductions, red for increases, blue for other changes. Each changed cell shows the original value (strikethrough) above the proposed value.
- **Legend** explaining the color coding
- **Accept Changes** button — applies the controller's proposed values and advances the CR (to CC Owner if resource changes, or directly to approved)
- **Decline and Resubmit** button — resets the CR back to pending_controller_approval for the PL to resubmit with their own modifications

**Normal CRs:** Non-sent-back CRs expand to show a tabular detail view grid with monthly comparison data, KPI strip, justification, and a 'View Full Detail' button.

See `docs/workflows/04-change-requests.md` (W04.4 send-back round-trip; W04.5 browse) for the full walks.

sections.title: System Suggestions
sections.body: The system analyzes spending patterns and generates suggestions during Phase 2 of the forecast wizard. Types include trend-based adjustments, burn rate projections, actuals-based corrections, and utilization insights. System-suggested changes are flagged in the resulting CR for controller transparency.

sections.title: Project Submission Workflow
sections.body:
New projects follow a multi-step submission lifecycle:

**1. Create Draft:** Project Lead clicks **+ New** in the project list, fills in project details and an optional resource plan with monthly hour allocations. The project is saved as 'draft' status.

**2. Submit for Review:** PL clicks **Submit** to send the draft for CC Owner confirmation. The forecast snapshot is saved as the 'original' submission. Status becomes 'pending_cc_confirmation'.

**3. CC Owner Confirmation:** The CC Owner reviews and confirms resource availability (using the Resource Assignment grid in Capacity Management). Status moves to 'pending_approval'.

**4. Controller Review:** The controller reviews the submission in the Portfolio Overview Intake Queue. They can Approve (project becomes active), Reject (back to draft), or Request Changes (opens editable forecast grid to propose modifications).

**5. Changes Requested:** If the controller requests changes, the PL sees an amber banner in the Workbench with the controller's feedback. The PL can 'Review Proposed Changes' to see a diff view, then 'Accept Changes' or 'Edit and Resubmit'.

The full lifecycle from intake Stage 0 to operate Stage 5 is documented in `docs/workflows/02-project-lifecycle.md`.

sections.title: Backlog Scoring
sections.body:
Projects in the Backlog (Stage 0-2 candidates) are ranked by a composite score combining a Tech Navigator profile (Complexity 30% × Value Creation 70% per `[A-TN-01..09]`). The Tech Navigator card on the Overview tab summarises the three scores; the deeper edit surface lives in the Backlog detail page (`/backlog/<project-id>`) via the Scores & Ranking tab.

Each project also carries a **t-shirt size** (XS / S / M / L / XL) derived from `total_budget` against thresholds in `PlanningParameter` (`tech_navigator` group). Resizing the budget reclassifies the t-shirt and re-ranks the backlog.

Sub-criteria scored 1-5 each:
- **Complexity** (3 sub-scores, weighted 40% / 40% / 20%): Standardization / Usage / Maintenance
- **Value Creation** (3 sub-scores, weighted 50% / 40% / 10%): Financial / Payback / Competitive
- 2 reserved sub-criterion slots for future configurable factors

The full Tech Navigator scoring rubric is in `docs/workflows/11-tech-navigator-and-backlog.md` (W11.1).

sections.title: Changes Requested Banner
sections.body:
When a controller requests changes to a submitted project, the Project Lead sees an amber notification banner at the top of the project workspace. The banner shows the controller's feedback text and provides two actions:

- **Review Proposed Changes** — opens a diff view comparing the PL's original submission against the controller's proposed changes, with changed cells highlighted
- **Edit and Resubmit** — opens the forecast grid for the PL to make their own adjustments before resubmitting

The same diff view is also accessible from the Intake Queue in Portfolio Overview by clicking 'Open Full Detail' on a project with 'changes_requested' status.

sections.title: Change Request Workflow
sections.body:
Change requests follow a multi-step lifecycle:

**1. PL Submits CR:** During the monthly forecast review (5-phase wizard), the Project Lead's Phase 5 Submit creates one or more CRs. Each CR partitions by affected CC. While any CR is pending, the forecast review button is locked to prevent overlapping submissions.

**2. CC Owner Confirmation (if internal resource changes):** When a CR has internal resource changes, it routes first to the CC Owner. The CC Owner sees delta-based requests showing the change direction (Increase / Decrease badge), the delta hours, the original allocation, the resulting total, and who is currently allocated to that role. The CC Owner can confirm, partially fulfill, counter-propose, or decline.

**3. Controller Review:** The Controller sees pending CRs in the Portfolio Overview CR Approvals tab. They can:
- **Approve** — CR is approved; live forecast is updated; new ForecastVersion (`version_type='cr_approval'`) is written.
- **Reject** — CR is rejected with a required reason.
- **Request Changes** — Controller opens an editable grid to adjust specific values (hours, amounts) and sends back with feedback.

**4. PL Reviews Sent-Back Changes:** The PL sees the sent-back CR in their Change History with an amber 'Action Required' badge. Expanding it shows a diff view comparing original vs controller-proposed values with color-coded cells. The PL can:
- **Accept Changes** — applies the controller's proposed values
- **Decline and Resubmit** — resets CR to pending_controller_approval

**Final state:** Approved CRs update the project's forecast data and write an immutable ForecastVersion. The full audit trail is visible in the Change History tab. See `docs/workflows/04-change-requests.md` for the four CR walks (draft, CC confirm, approve, send-back).
